summary: The note is an autumn-focused guide to farm-to-table eating, covering the seasonal produce calendar, shopping tips for farmers' markets, preservation techniques, recipes, and the community and health benefits of local food. It draws on quotes from local farmers, an orchard owner, a dietitian, and a chef. Its central message is that simple preparation of fresh, seasonal, local ingredients yields the best flavor, nutrition, and community support.
one_line: A guide to autumn farm-to-table eating that covers seasonal produce, market shopping, preserving, recipes, and community and health benefits.
key_facts: As of September 15, 2023, farmer Emilie Jacobsen of Jacobsen's Fresh Farms has begun harvesting the last summer crops (tomatoes, sweet corn, bell peppers) and is transitioning to root vegetables and hearty greens.
Autumn offerings named by Jacobsen include squashes, potatoes, pumpkins, and leafy greens like kale; the note quotes her under the name 'Jacobs' while she picks a butternut squash.
Local agricultural expert Dr. Marcus Richardson advises residents to consult seasonal charts at farmers' markets or online to learn which produce is locally available through the year.
Squash varieties starring in autumn are acorn, spaghetti, and butternut; apples and pears reach peak sweetness and suit both savory and sweet dishes.
Orchard owner Sophia Martinelli says her orchard is 'ablaze with activity' in autumn and encourages people to visit, taste, and learn about different varietals.
Autumn mushrooms include button, shiitake, and porcini, which pair with Swiss chard and Brussels sprouts.
On October 3, 2023, dietitian and local-food advocate Laura Thompson advised shoppers to look for vibrant colors and hearty textures, since fall produce should feel firm and heavy for its size.
Shoppers are advised to arrive at the farmers' market early, when selection is richest, and to ask farmers like Erik Gunderson for cooking advice and farming details.
On November 12, 2023, chef Anita Rivera will host a preservation workshop at the Greenway Culinary Institute covering canning, pickling, and fermenting.
Suggested autumn recipes are roasted butternut squash soup, caramelized pear and gorgonzola pizza, and wild mushroom risotto.
Laura Thompson says seasonal produce is packed with antioxidants, vitamins, and minerals, and she served kale and roasted pumpkin salad samples at a local health fair.
The note frames farm-to-table as a socio-economic relationship that supports the local economy and community resilience, and stresses simple cooking that lets ingredients shine.
